correctness.rationale: The six permutation exponent vectors give a rank-five augmented lattice and a primitive parity binomial. Differentiating gives a saturated squarefree ideal whose nine minimal line primes exhaust all singular points. Its tensor-product Stanley--Reisner ring has Hilbert series (1+2t)^2/(1-t)^2, implying the arithmetic genus and Cohen--Macaulayness. Local charts are uv-wz=0 times a smooth parameter or ab-cde=0; the toric height-one divisor relation matrix has rank four, primitive image and quotient Z^2 at all six vertices, while transverse nodes yield Z along open lines. Hypersurface S2 and singular codimension three imply normality. The packaged standard-library checker freshly reproduced all 64 binary supports, finite Hilbert terms, lattice rank, divisor-matrix minors, and node Hessian. The proof, not finite tests, covers all points.

originality.rationale: The classical cubic toric equation and toric divisor sequence are explicitly excluded from the new contribution. The compared full-text Birkhoff papers identify the polytope, its toric binomial and faces but do not give this complete scheme-theoretic singular curve with local Weil class-group jumps. A relevant published K_{3,3} curve occurs in another deformation-theoretic construction, not as the singular scheme of this Birkhoff toric cubic. The full novel package is the Birkhoff-specific reduced Jacobian scheme, Cohen--Macaulay Hilbert data, transverse types, and explicit local class groups. Incomplete indexing and differently phrased classical proofs remain risks.
residual_risks: The nine-line Stanley--Reisner K3,3 curve is already known as an abstract variety in the Wan Kuranishi result; only the specific identification and complementary local divisor geometry are asserted as new.
Complete full text of the Wan published entry was not accessible; a hidden equivalence cannot be ruled out.
The Birkhoff cubic is classical, so an unindexed explicit Jacobian/class-group computation could already exist.
This is a self-review rather than independent publication or peer review.

value.rationale: The 3x3 Birkhoff polytope is the canonical smallest nontrivial transportation polytope with a primitive cubic circuit. The complete nonreduced-versus-reduced singular-scheme determination, K3,3 incidence with degree and arithmetic genus, and jump of the local divisor-class-group rank at all six intersections supply natural scheme-theoretic and birational invariants of its toric embedding. This is a coherent classification of all singular closed points and class groups, not a rephrasing of the defining cubic or a cherry-picked numerical example; class-group ranks constrain local factoriality and toric resolutions.
